timeline: You would not expect sticky syrup to outrun you, but the 1919 Boston wave moved at 35 MPH and flattened steel girders.
People enjoyed the warm winter afternoon.
Inside, expanding gas built deadly pressure.
Bystanders mistook the growl for trains.
Ripping rivets fired like machine guns.
A massive wave surged through Boston.
Cooling syrup trapped people in rubble.
Cadets waded in to drag survivors out.
The disaster became a milestone for corporate regulation.
For decades after, hot summer days still smelled sweet.
